stats.metric: Change in references to 'DEI', 'diversity' and 'racial equity' in Fortune 100 companies' public documents
stats.caption: drop in references to “DEI,” “diversity” and “racial equity” in Fortune 100 companies’ public documents, January 2023 to May 2025.
stats.source: Rich McEachran, "Why is big tech rolling back DEI initiatives?" ITPro, Oct. 30, 2025, citing Gravity Research
stats.notes: Article text: 'References to terms including ‘DEI’, ‘diversity’, and ‘racial equity’ fell 72% in the public documents of Fortune 100 companies between January 2023 and May 2025, per Gravity Research data.' The analysis covered DEI, ESG and sustainability reports, earnings calls and SEC filings, and 'tracked a 98% decline in the term ‘DEI’ itself.' This measures language, not programs or hiring; Gravity Research's own report was not opened.

stats.metric: Share of companies that had completely abandoned DEI efforts
stats.group: Respondents to LeadDev's Engineering Leadership Report 2025
stats.caption: of companies in LeadDev’s 2025 Engineering Leadership Report had completely abandoned DEI efforts. Most of the pullback is quieter.
stats.source: Chantal Kapani, "DEI crackdown sparks quiet tech rollback," LeadDev, Aug. 14, 2025, reporting LeadDev's Engineering Leadership Report 2025
stats.notes: Article text: 'according to LeadDev’s Engineering Leadership Report 2025, only 5% of companies have completely abandoned DEI efforts. The report found that a majority of respondents (56%) still view DEI as an organizational priority, while 18% believe these initiatives are being deprioritized. Meanwhile, 14% said DEI was never a priority ... and 7% reported that their organizations are actually increasing their focus.' The 'quieter' reading comes from Jessie Auguste, software engineer at CybSafe, quoted in the article: companies are 'quietly defunding them, reducing headcount, and letting initiatives ‘sunset’ without replacement.' The survey's sample size and makeup are not given in the article. The brief's URL (leaddev.com/?p=27681) redirects to this article.

note.title: The diversity reports that tracked tech hiring have stopped
note.text: Google, Meta and Microsoft confirmed in 2025 that they would not publish diversity data that year. Google had published 11 annual reports in a row. Those reports were one of the few public records of who gets hired in tech and at what level, so stage 06 outcomes are now harder to track.

source.cite: "Google, Meta, And Microsoft Quietly End Diversity Reporting As DEI Pullback Widens," Allwork.Space, Nov. 7, 2025, citing Wired

note.notes: Article text: 'Google, Microsoft, and Meta have confirmed they will not publish diversity, equity, and inclusion (DEI) data this year.' and Google had published '11 consecutive annual reports.' It does not say the companies stopped permanently. Verified for the rollback timeline on 2026-11-20.

supporters.label: What supporters of the corporate changes argue
supporters.quote: Far too many employers defend certain types of race or sex preferences as good, provided they are motivated by business interests in ‘diversity, equity, or inclusion.’ But no matter an employer’s motive, there is no ‘good,’ or even acceptable, race or sex discrimination.
supporters.who: Andrea Lucas, Acting Chair of the U.S. Equal Employment Opportunity Commission, March 19, 2025

source.cite: EEOC and Justice Department Warn Against Unlawful DEI-Related Discrimination, Mar. 19, 2025

outcome.label: What the outcome data shows
outcome.text: Who gets hired in tech, at what level and for what pay, by race and gender, since these changes. Not yet collected, and harder to find now that the largest companies have stopped publishing diversity reports.

companies.title: Meta
companies.finding: In January 2025, Meta ended its DEI team, its representation goals and the “diverse slate approach” in hiring. An internal memo tied the changes to the “legal and policy landscape” for DEI in the United States.
companies.apa: Johnson, L. (2025, January 14). Meta joins chorus of DEI rollbacks, cutting roles and programs. *HR Dive*.
companies.notes: Article: Meta will "cease to incorporate the ‘diverse slate approach’ in its hiring processes, according to changes first reported Friday by Axios"; the memo attributed the changes to the "legal and policy landscape surrounding diversity, equity and inclusion efforts in the United States." The diverse slate change is sourced to Axios; the supplier diversity change was confirmed by a Meta spokesperson.

companies.title: Google
companies.finding: In February 2025, Google told employees it was scrapping some of its diversity hiring targets. As a federal contractor, it said it was reviewing changes required by “recent court decisions and executive orders.”
companies.apa: Liedtke, M. (2025, February 6). Google scraps diversity hiring goals in the face of Trump’s new anti-DEI government contractor rules. *Fortune*.
companies.notes: Article: "Google is scrapping some of its diversity hiring targets"; Google’s statement says its teams are "evaluating changes required following recent court decisions and executive orders on this topic." Associated Press story carried by Fortune.

companies.title: Amazon
companies.finding: In a Dec. 16, 2024 memo, Amazon said it was “winding down outdated programs and materials” after reviewing hundreds of initiatives, and would focus on “programs with proven outcomes.” The memo did not say which programs were cut.
companies.apa: Amazon to halt some of its DEI programs: Internal memo. (2025, January 10). *NBC4 Washington* (CNBC).
companies.notes: Article: "In a Dec. 16 internal note to staffers that was obtained by CNBC, Candi Castleberry, Amazon’s VP of inclusive experiences and technology, said the company was in the process of ‘winding down outdated programs and materials’"; "Castleberry’s memo doesn’t say which programs the company is dropping." Memo text: aiming to complete that "by the end of 2024."

companies.title: Microsoft
companies.finding: Microsoft did not publish a 2025 diversity report after releasing one every year since 2019. It said it had moved to “stories, videos, and insights that show inclusion in action.”
companies.apa: Moon, M. (2025, November 22). Microsoft isn’t releasing a diversity report for 2025. *Engadget*.
companies.notes: Statement from chief communications officer Frank Shaw: "We are not doing a traditional report this year as we’ve evolved beyond that to formats that are more dynamic and accessible — stories, videos, and insights that show inclusion in action." Engadget credits the original report to Stephen Totilo of Game File. Separately, Microsoft cut some DEI roles in July 2024; reports disagree on how many, so that is not used here.

programs.title: Diversity internships and early-career programs that ended or changed
programs.note: Only programs with a source that says what changed are listed. One so far.

rows.program: Meta University (10-week program for college freshmen and sophomores)
rows.change: Took its final class in 2025 and is closing. A Meta spokesperson confirmed it had accepted its final class.
rows.notes: Colleen Connolly, "With Meta University's Closure, a Sign of Changing Times in Tech," Work Shift, Apr. 30, 2025. Text: 'Meta will soon bring in the last cohort of students at Meta University, its diversity-focused training program that had been a model for the industry.' 'Tracy Clayton, a spokesperson for Meta, confirmed that Meta University has accepted its final class.' 'Then on Jan. 10, Meta sent out a memo indicating the closure of the training program.' 'Meta University was for freshmen and sophomores.' 'Within the last year, language on the website changed from targeting “students from underrepresented communities” to “students with a range of backgrounds, experiences and perspectives.”' The article does not give the number of students served or say whether a replacement program exists. Searched Nov 22, 2026 for other tech companies' internship or early-career programs ended, renamed or opened to all since January 2025; found none with a source that says so. Not included: Google Women Techmakers (moved to Technovation in Oct. 2025, a community program, not an internship) and Hack.Diversity (a nonprofit, not a company).
